span.p:
both implemented from day one (D29)
so Thai quality can be COMPARED on the same
golden set rather than argued about

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
no LangChain, no agent framework (D31)
What we actually need is: render a versioned prompt,
call an HTTP endpoint, parse JSON into a pydantic model,
retry, record cost and latency. That is ~200 lines we
fully control, versus a dependency that hides the
prompt, hides the retry, and breaks on upgrade.
Revisit trigger is written down: if we ever need real
multi-step tool use, reopen the decision.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the hard rule (D16)
coverage figures, eligibility and prices are DATA.
The model may summarise, classify and rank -
it may never PRODUCE a number. Hallucinating
a room-and-board limit is not a bad answer,
it is a mis-selling incident.
